title: Reservoir-prefill Sampler: kernel-probing model routing and reversible fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, kernel-aware prefill sampler that probes candidate model variants and kernel codepaths prior to committing to a full speculative decode. The sampler ("reservoir prober") issues short prefill probes (1-8 tokens) against a tiny reservoir of live requests to measure: kernel latency, attention memory behavior, KV cache pressure, and early acceptance signals.

Goals:
- Route the main request to the lowest-latency compatible variant under current kernel constraints.
- Produce calibrated acceptance metrics (per-probe confidence, KL divergence vs. golden prefix, top-k overlap) to decide early commit.
- Provide a reversible, low-cost fallback that can safely switch to a fallback model variant without losing coherence or violating SLOs.

Design highlights:
- Reservoir sampling: select up to N live candidate requests (configurable) each second to run 2–3 short prefills against top candidate model variants. This keeps probe cost bounded while maintaining representative workload sampling.
- Kernel-probing: probes record kernel-level timings (attention kernel choice, GEMM path, quantization path), KV allocation deltas, and decode head latency. This informs kernel-selection policies in router.
- Acceptance scoring: composite score combining normalized latency delta, prefix LM-score delta, and top-k overlap. Scores are fed to the routing decision with configurable thresholds and a short smoothing window.
- Reversible fallback: do not irrevocably commit tokens until acceptance passes a configurable window (e.g., 4 tokens). If acceptance fails, roll back by replaying the confirmed prefix against fallback variant with a soft-commit mechanism that re-emits only missing tokens to the client (or uses token-level edit fallback for streaming clients).
- Batching integration: probes piggyback on existing batching infrastructure; they are tagged low-priority and can be preempted by production batches.

Telemetry & metrics:
- New metrics: probe_latency_ms, probe_kernel_path, probe_kv_delta, acceptance_score, acceptance_pass_rate, rollback_rate, fallback_latency_cost.
- Dashboards: per-model and per-kernel heatmaps; 95/99 latency regressions for acceptance pass vs. fallback.
- Bench harness: synthetic workload driver + 1 week shadow sampling on hosted traffic.

Trade-offs & mitigations:
- Extra cost from probes: mitigate via small reservoir, low probe frequency, and piggyback batching.
- Latency tail risk when switching variants mid-decode: mitigation via soft-commit protocol and conservative smoothing thresholds.
- Metric calibration complexity across models: initially restrict to a candidate set (2 variants) and expand after calibration.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement probe instrumentation and local kernel-timing SDK (runtime-1.20) behind feature-flag (dev-only).
2) Internal perf tests + synthetic bench (2 sprints).
3) Shadow sampling on 1% traffic with canary routing (monitor acceptance_pass_rate, rollback_rate).
4) Gradual ramp and dashboarding; enable for broader fleet after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.

Open decisions:
- Default acceptance score weights (latency vs. generation match).
- Soft-commit window size vs. customer-visible streaming semantics.

Risks & rollback:
- If rollback_rate > 2% on canary, disable speculative routing and revert to single-model decode; notify customers with traffic-affecting SLA.

Acceptance scoring function is implemented with default weights and unit tests
Soft-commit rollback mechanism preserves client stream coherence in >= 99% of shadow traffic tests
